findings.summary: In the producer loop, rule (c) checks the snapshot's ci.yml against the running binary's compiled BUILD_PATHS, not the status.rs in the work tree, which gives false send-backs and misses real drift.
findings.evidence: Decision 2 says 'the rule data is the compiled constant' and 'Reading the constant directly means no parsing of status.rs'. Decision 6 runs check_all on the producer's snapshot from the installed Athena binary. That binary's constant comes from whatever commit it was built from (status.rs stale_build_line exists because the installed build can lag behind the checkout). So: (1) a producer that correctly adds a glob to every athena-bin key and to BUILD_PATHS in status.rs is sent back, because the old constant lacks it, and the producer cannot fix that; (2) a producer that edits BUILD_PATHS in status.rs alone is not caught in the loop; (3) an installed build older than a BUILD_PATHS change at the base sends back every job on Athena's tree. Only the athena-cli repo test, where the compiled constant matches the tree, is sound. Fix: Make rule (c) read BUILD_PATHS from the mirror file it names. Parse the `pub const BUILD_PATHS` array in the snapshot's crates/athena-core/src/status.rs (syn is already an athena-core dependency, or use a narrow line parse). Add a repo-test assertion that the parsed list equals status::BUILD_PATHS. Or mark the rule repo-test-only and skip it in mirror_drift_in. Either way, consider sending back only drift that is new against the base, so drift already present at the base is never charged to the producer.
findings.location: Decision 2 / Decision 6: Rule::HashFilesCover(&status::BUILD_PATHS) run by mirror_drift_in in run/producer.rs

findings.summary: README.md line 193 also lists the five build paths, and the dependents list leaves it out.
findings.evidence: Grep for the five-path phrase finds README.md:193: 'a change under `crates/`, `xtask/`, `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` or `setup.sh` since the commit it was built from'. That sentence describes the drain's stale-build refusal, which uses BUILD_PATHS. The plan edits main.rs:261 and drain.rs:137 because they 'would be the same kind of stale hand-kept copy', but not README.md. The CHANGELOG.md lines 129 and 1652 and D-entry line 3645 are history that must not be edited, so they can stay. Fix: Add README.md to Files and Dependents, and reword line 193 to name BUILD_PATHS or list the nine roots. D158 should also say that the earlier decision at docs/decisions.md line 3645 lists five paths and is now outdated, since that text cannot be edited.
findings.location: Dependents: 'prose copy of the BUILD_PATHS list'; Decision 8

findings.summary: A send-back for drift alone starts with an intro about unmet criteria and planned files, and its 'goes to the verifier' promise does not hold for drift.
findings.evidence: In send_back.rs, send_back_text_scoped (lines 134-171) gives each extra reason (scope, gate, replay) a leading sentence: 'When no criteria ... are listed, that ... is the only reason for this send-back'. With drift only, the match falls to `(None, None, None) => send_back_text(...)`, whose intro reads 'Your previous report did not show every acceptance criterion as met...'. The wrapper only adds a section at the end. Fix: Have append_mirror_drift also put one leading sentence before the intro, as the gate, replay and scope reasons do. Or say in D158 why the general intro is enough. Assert the sentence in the mirrors_ loop test.

findings.summary: The plan keeps the uncovered-line message 'unchanged', yet the demonstration expects it to name docs/ontology.toml and 'add a senses entry'.
findings.evidence: The existing message at ontology.rs lines 424-427 is '{name}: {path}:{n} names the term as a definition or role and no sense or excuse covers it: {line}'. It names neither the mirror file nor a fix. Fix: Say that check_entry wraps each message in a Drift that names the mirror (docs/ontology.toml) and the fix ('add a senses entry or an excuse'), with the inner text unchanged. Assert the wrapped text, not the inner one.

findings.summary: Snapshot::base() returns Option<&str>, so the call as written does not compile.
findings.evidence: crates/athena-git/src/snapshot.rs line 131 is `pub fn base(&self) -> Option<&str>`. Git::show_file (lib.rs line 453) takes &str and returns Result<Option<Vec<u8>>>. Fix: Build the base closure only when base() is Some, and return None otherwise, which skips rule (b).

findings.summary: editing() adds the same edits on every producer turn, so it cannot express 'fix on the send-back'.
findings.evidence: run/tests.rs lines 2234-2247: editing extends turn.edits with `extra` on every Producer call. reconciling_on_send_back (line 2288) is the existing pattern that adds edits only when the prompt contains '## Sent back'. Fix: Name a script modelled on reconciling_on_send_back that adds the xtask/shard-timings.txt line only when the prompt carries '## Sent back'.
findings.location: Demonstration 3: loop test 'a producer that adds the timings line on the send-back'

summary: I checked the plan's claims in the snapshot with Read and Grep. Round 3 holds up well. The code it builds on is real: the producer self-check and send-back match in run/producer.rs (lines 285-423), the run/tests.rs helpers (repo, commit_file, editing, governed_job_with, and reconciling_on_send_back as the send-back pattern), Snapshot::git/base/dir and Git::show_file, and the full ontology walk in crates/athena-cli/tests/ontology.rs. The BUILD_PATHS drift is real too: athena.toml is compiled in as athena-gate BUILTIN_CONFIG, docs/system-facts.md as briefs.rs SYSTEM_FACTS, and every athena-bin key hashes all nine globs. Two problems keep this at revise. First, rule (c) compares the snapshot's ci.yml with the BUILD_PATHS constant compiled into the running binary. In the producer loop that binary is the installed Athena, not the tree being edited, so a correct change to both files is sent back, and an installed build older than the base sends back every Athena job. Second, README.md line 193 repeats the five-path list. The plan fixes the same kind of copy in main.rs and drain.rs but omits this one from its dependents. Smaller points: a send-back for drift alone gets an intro about criteria; the ontology message is kept unchanged yet the demonstration expects it to name the fix; snapshot.base() returns an Option; and editing() cannot change its edits on the second turn.
